newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ezz Group sees Egyptian construction growing 10 pcT.
newsitem.headline: Ezz Group sees Egyptian construction growing 10 pcT.

text.p: Egypt's construction sector will grow at 10 percent a year for the next few years, even faster if the government lifts restrictions on real estate mortgages, the chairman of the Ezz Group said on Monday.

Chairman Ahmed Ezz, whose group is one of the country's largest private-sector producer of construction materials including steel and ceramics, told Reuters in an interview he thought it had already achieved this rate of growth but unlicensed building concealed this from official figures.

"You feel you have this stable macroeconomic environment that is very conducive to growth... In the construction market and related industries one should comfortably assume growth of 10 percent annually over the next few years," Ezz added.
The Ezz Group has invested heavily in the sector. It now produces 700,000 tonnes of steel a year and holds 25 percent of the Egyptian market for building steel.
Its latest projects include a 700,000 tonne a year melt shop to feed the company's downstream plants and a one million tonne a year flat steel plant near the town of Suez.
The melt shop will start work in April or May while the flat steel plant, a joint venture with Danieli of Italy and other investors, will open in late 1999 or early 2000.
Ezz said the biggest single boost to the construction sector would come from changes in the banking law, which in its present form prevents banks repossessing residential property.
Because of the regulations few Egyptians can acquire flats or houses without paying most of the cost before moving in.

"I believe we will see this changed very soon with the total change in the policy makers and the ideas we have been seeing," said Ezz, referring to the government's widely acclaimed economic reform programme.

"This will affect the sector dramatically because one of our biggest problems is the housing problem and, with a substantial portion of the population, perhaps 20 percent, now having a per capita income of $4,000 or $5,000, there is room for huge growth in this sector if the vehicle for financing low to medium cost housing is available," he added.
Other factors stimulating construction are the tourism boom of the past two years and the release of land for building around Cairo and other towns, he said.
